BAGAS PRATAMA — Backend Engineer, 6 years.
EXPERIENCE: 2021-2026 Payments Platform Engineer. Owned a Go service handling 4k req/s; cut p99 latency from 420ms to 160ms by replacing an N+1 query pattern and adding a Redis read-through cache. Designed the Postgres schema for a ledger of 180M rows (partitioned by month, tuned autovacuum, cut slow queries by 70%). Ran the Kubernetes migration for 12 services and set up GitHub Actions with parallel integration tests (build time 22m -> 6m). Earlier: 2019-2021 Go microservices for a logistics startup; introduced contract tests that reduced staging incidents by half.
SKILLS: Go (expert), Postgres, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, gRPC, observability (Prometheus/Grafana).
report_text:
CASE STUDY: reducing checkout failures.
Problem: 3.4% of checkout attempts failed in peak hours, costing an estimated Rp120M/month. Constraint: no downtime, one engineer, 6 weeks.
Approach: instrumented the flow with tracing, found the failure concentrated in one downstream provider call with a 5s timeout and no circuit breaker. Rejected the obvious 'increase timeout' fix because it shifted the failure to connection exhaustion; instead added a breaker with a 200ms budget and idempotent retries.
Results: failures 3.4% -> 0.6% measured over 4 weeks with 1.2M checkouts; p99 checkout latency 1.8s -> 640ms. Wrote a post-mortem and a runbook; the breaker became the standard pattern for 5 other integrations.
